bib.title: MEDAGENTS: Large Language Models as Collaborators for Zero-shot Medical Reasoning
bib.venue: Findings of the Association for Computational Linguistics: ACL 2024, pages 599-621

read.skipped: Reference list skimmed; Appendix B case-study tables (Tables 9-11) not read in detail

question: Can role-playing LLM agents holding a multi-disciplinary consultation improve zero-shot medical question answering without training or retrieval?
hypothesis: Role-playing agents from different medical disciplines, discussing until consensus, surface latent medical knowledge and improve reasoning over CoT and self-consistency.
contributions: First multi-agent framework in the medical domain, with consensus through multi-agent communication
Role-playing gives faithfulness and interpretability and reasons with accurate knowledge without RAG
Experiments on nine datasets, plus error categorisation by human evaluation

method.summary: Training-free five-stage pipeline: recruit question and option domain experts, each writes analyses, a summary report is made, experts vote yes/no and propose edits until unanimous (max 5 rounds), then a decision maker picks the answer. Run on GPT-3.5-Turbo and GPT-4.

datasets.name: MMLU medical subtasks (anatomy, clinical knowledge, college medicine, medical genetics, professional medicine, college biology)
datasets.source: Hendrycks et al. 2020, following Singhal et al. 2023a

inference.samples: One run on 300 sampled examples per dataset; 5 repetitions in App E for MedQA and MedMCQA; SC uses 5 samples
inference.prompting: Zero-shot; role system prompts and guideline prompts per stage (Table 12)

metrics.name: Accuracy
metrics.definition: fraction of multiple-choice questions answered correctly

eval.protocol: Single sampled subset of 300 per dataset; no significance test; error analysis by human categorisation of 40 error cases

prompts.text: Here is a medical report: synthesized_report. As a medical expert specialized in domain, please carefully read the report and decide whether your opinions are consistent with this report. Please respond only with: [YES or NO].
Here is a synthesized report: syn_report. Based on the above report, select the optimal choice to answer the question.
prompts.where: Table 12, promptdm (truncated; full text in the table)

evidence.quote: We randomly sample 300 examples for each dataset and conduct experiments on them.

results.claim: MedAgents (GPT-4) averages 86.7 across nine datasets vs 83.0 for zero-shot CoT+SC and 80.6 zero-shot
results.setup: Nine medical QA sets, 300 random examples each, zero-shot, temperature 1.0, top_p 1.0, GPT-4 via Azure

results.claim: MedAgents (GPT-3.5) averages 72.1 vs 70.9 for zero-shot CoT+SC and 71.6 for few-shot CoT+SC
results.setup: Nine medical QA sets, 300 random examples each, zero-shot, temperature 1.0, top_p 1.0, GPT-3.5-Turbo

results.claim: On MedQA, MedAgents with GPT-4 reaches 83.7 vs 74.5 zero-shot CoT+SC and 82.9 few-shot CoT+SC
Zero-shot CoT lowers accuracy below plain zero-shot for GPT-3.5 (avg 58.3 vs 67.8) and on MedQA GPT-4 (61.8 vs 73.0)
results.table: Table 2, GPT-3.5 Zero-shot CoT, column Avg.

results.setup: MedQA, ablation of MedAgents stages (model and sample count not stated for this table)

results.claim: Cost of the method is about $1.41 per 100 QA examples and about 40s per example
results.quote: the cost of our method is $1.41 for 100 QA examples (about ¢1.4 per question) and the inference time per example is about 40s

results.claim: Same-domain agents are worse than six different domains: 6 different 64.1 vs 6 same 59.2, 5 same 57.5, 4 same 55.9 on MedQA
results.note: Same-domain accuracy falls with fewer agents (59.2, 57.5, 55.9)
results.table: Table 7, row w/ 6 different domains, column MedQA

results.claim: Removing the least relevant domain expert raises MedQA accuracy (66.2) above the full set (63.8); removing the most relevant lowers it (60.5)
results.setup: GPT-3.5, only 20 samples, manual relevance labels
results.note: Full-pipeline value 63.8 here differs from 64.1 in Table 2 (20-sample subset)
results.table: Table 6, row Remove least relevant, column MedQA

results.claim: Any number of expert agents beats the baseline; optimal counts are 5 question and 2 option agents (4 question agents for PubMedQA)
results.setup: MedQA, question and option agent counts varied 1-8 and 1-5; read from Fig 3 and Table 5

results.claim: 77% of 40 sampled error cases come from lack or mis-retrieval of domain knowledge, 8% from CoT errors
results.setup: 40 error cases from MedQA and MedMCQA, human categorisation
results.quote: the majority (77%) of the error examples are due to confusion about the domain knowledge

results.claim: Repeated runs are stable: GPT-4 MedQA 83.7 single vs 83.5 over 5 repetitions
results.table: Table 13, row MC framework GPT-4 (5 repetitions), column MedQA

results.claim: Open-source medical models trail: MedAlpaca-7B gets 55.2 on MedQA vs 83.7 for MedAgents (GPT-4)

limits: Authors concede cost exceeds CoT or direct prompting
77% of errors are domain-knowledge gaps, a bottleneck the pipeline cannot fix
Only 300 samples per dataset, no seeds or significance tests; domain-relevance study on 20 samples
Ablation table 3 does not state the model or sample count

Same-domain agent comparison confounds agent count with domain diversity but uses same-domain duplicates, not equal-cost single-agent sampling; SC (5 samples) baseline is the only compute-matched-ish comparison and is not matched in cost
Medical QA benchmarks only; GPT-3.5/GPT-4 era
